template.name: Fixed Assets
template.description: Capital expenditure authorization, capital work in progress (CWIP), asset capitalization, depreciation, impairment, physical verification, transfers and disposals under IAS 16, IAS 36 and IFRS 16 (right-of-use assets).

risks.title: Capital expenditure is incurred without appropriate authorization or beyond approved budgets.
Costs are inappropriately capitalized (repairs, maintenance, training, abnormal costs) or capital costs are expensed, misstating assets and profit.
Completed projects remain in CWIP and are not transferred to fixed assets, delaying the start of depreciation.
Depreciation is calculated using incorrect useful lives, residual values, start dates or methods.
Assets recorded in the register do not physically exist, are lost or stolen, or exist but are not recorded.
Impairment indicators are not identified, or impairment is not measured in accordance with IAS 36.
Disposals and transfers are not authorized or not recorded, resulting in incorrect gains/losses and overstated assets.
Leases are not identified or right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are measured incorrectly under IFRS 16.

controls.title: Capital expenditure request (CER) approval
controls.description: All capital expenditure is authorized through a capital expenditure request stating business case, budget reference, estimated cost and expected useful life, approved per the DoA (Department Head up to SAR 250,000; CEO up to SAR 5 million; Board above). The ERP blocks capex purchase orders not linked to an approved CER and project code, and reports commitments against CER budget.

controls.title: Capitalization policy review of project costs
controls.description: The Fixed Asset Accountant reviews costs charged to each project monthly against the capitalization policy (directly attributable costs, borrowing costs on qualifying assets, exclusion of training, admin overheads and abnormal costs) and reclassifies non-qualifying costs to expense. Repairs and maintenance expense above SAR 50,000 per invoice is reviewed for items that should have been capitalized. The review is signed by the Financial Controller.

controls.title: CWIP ageing and capitalization review
controls.description: Finance reviews the CWIP ageing report monthly with project managers to identify projects that are substantially complete or available for use; completion certificates trigger transfer to the fixed asset register with the correct asset class, useful life and in-service date. Projects in CWIP over 12 months are reported to the CFO with justification.

controls.title: Asset master creation and depreciation parameters
controls.description: New assets are created in the fixed asset register by the Fixed Asset Accountant with asset class, cost, in-service date, useful life and residual value from the approved capitalization form; asset class defaults in the system drive useful life and depreciation method per the accounting policy, and any override requires Financial Controller approval.

controls.title: Depreciation run and reasonableness review
controls.description: Depreciation is calculated automatically by the fixed asset module in the monthly run. The Fixed Asset Accountant performs a reasonableness test (expected depreciation by asset class based on opening balance, additions and disposals versus actual) and investigates differences above 5%; the analysis is reviewed by the Financial Controller.

controls.title: Fixed asset register to GL reconciliation
controls.description: The fixed asset sub-ledger (cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value by class, and CWIP) is reconciled to the general ledger monthly; differences are investigated and cleared, and the reconciliation is reviewed and signed by the Financial Controller.

controls.title: Physical verification of fixed assets
controls.description: A physical verification of all tagged assets is performed annually (high-value and movable assets semi-annually) by a team independent of asset custodians, using the asset register and tagging system; discrepancies are investigated, approved for adjustment by the CFO, and the register is updated. Results are reported to the Audit Committee.

controls.title: Impairment indicator assessment
controls.description: At each reporting date, Finance completes an IAS 36 impairment indicator checklist (idle assets, obsolescence, physical damage, adverse market or regulatory changes, performance below plan) with input from operations; where indicators exist, a recoverable amount assessment (value in use or fair value less costs of disposal) is prepared and reviewed by the CFO, with key assumptions documented.

controls.title: Asset disposal and transfer authorization
controls.description: Disposals, write-offs and inter-location transfers require an asset disposal/transfer form approved per the DoA (Department Head and Finance Manager; CFO for net book value above SAR 100,000), with sale proceeds supported by an approved sale process or auction. The Fixed Asset Accountant records the disposal in the register in the month of approval and calculates the gain or loss.

controls.title: Lease identification and IFRS 16 measurement
controls.description: Procurement and Legal notify Finance of all new, modified or terminated contracts containing the right to use an identified asset via the contract register; Finance assesses each contract against IFRS 16, records the lease in the lease accounting tool with term, payments and incremental borrowing rate, and the Financial Controller reviews the lease schedule and quarterly roll-forward of ROU assets and lease liabilities.

controls.title: Restricted access to the fixed asset register
controls.description: Access to create, modify or retire assets and to change depreciation parameters in the fixed asset module is restricted to the Fixed Asset Accountant and Finance Systems roles; access is reviewed quarterly by the Financial Controller.
